Q: When using slurm, how do I instruct it to use a different number of tasks per node? Heterogeneous jobs don't seem to work A:

I've encountered a similar issue. I have a single-process application with a massive memory footprint, but since our Slurm cluster allocates memory on a per-CPU basis, I’m forced to request all 64 CPUs while simultaneously limiting the process count to 16 per node.

My approach involves using OMP_NUM_THREADS (or whatever name you like) to define the CPU allocation per MPI rank. I then leverage Slurm's environment variables to dynamically calculate the tasks-per-node and core-binding requirements, passing these to mpirun via the --map-by flag. By adjusting OMP_NUM_THREADS, I can throttle the process density: for instance, setting it to 1 yields 64 processes per node (64/1), while setting it to 4 scales it down to 16 (64/4). Below is the shell script implementation:

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --nodes=4               
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=64  
#SBATCH --partition=cpu
#SBATCH --mem=250G

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=4
export OPENBLAS_DEFAULT_NUM_THREADS=$OMP_NUM_THREADS
NP_PER_NODE=$(( $SLURM_NTASKS_PER_NODE / $OMP_NUM_THREADS ))
NP_ALL=$(( $SLURM_NNODES * $NP_PER_NODE  ))


mpirun -n $NP_ALL \
  --map-by ppr:$NP_PER_NODE:node:pe=$OMP_NUM_THREADS \
  --bind-to core \
  --report-bindings \
  <cmd args ...>
